newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends quiet day down, but mood bullish.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends quiet day down, but mood bullish.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed Thursday's lacklustre session lower, but many traders remained bullish in the near term.
Benchmark May closed down three stg at 1,044 stg per tonne and July lost three stg to 1,058 after surging on Wednesday to about 7-1/2 month highs.
Despite the losses, many traders said the market still looked bullish, with July poised to test resistance between 1,100 and 1,150 stg in the next week and a half.
They said Thursday's action was merely a consolidation of recent gains as investors stepped aside to reassess the strong rally on Wednesday.

But some analysts and traders doubted cocoa prices could climb much higher in the very near term because of forecasts for falls in European grind data due this week and next and expected liquidation or rollover from speculators of May positions before the first notice day on April 17 in New York.
However, bullish traders said speculative May selling or rolling of positions into July would only have a negligible effect on the market in the very short-term.
They also said expectations for European grind data were already being factored into the market and that weak data could end up either having little effect or even a positive effect on prices.

Broker GNI said: "While there is a general feeling that they (European grind figures) will fail to match the impressive figures of last year, increased processed imports from origin are showing that underlying consumption remains robust."
Origin sales, which helped cap prices earlier this year, were also nearly complete for the main crop and not likely to keep a lid on gains, a trader said.
Markets had little reaction to news Ghana will end its 1996/97 main crop cocoa purchasing season at the close of business on Thursday but final returns on purchases will be accepted until April 17.
Total cocoa volume was sluggish with 4,214 contracts changing hands.

Traders said arbitrage activity was thinner this week due to the wider time difference with New York after London's clocks moved forward last weekend for daylight savings time. The United States will move forward an hour for daylight savings time this weekend. -- Medora Lee, London newsdesk +44 171 542 8072
